decisions.reason: The product has already demonstrated strong external adoption and is tightly aligned with the firm's core border and passenger-processing capabilities, so its option value is largely realized and there is little reason to exit.

After two years without visible traction, a travel health requirements API looks less attractive as demand uncertainty has likely resolved downward and the firm can redeploy resources to stronger compliance and verification offers.
This training module is close to the firm's existing training business and likely inexpensive to maintain, so management would keep the option open despite limited market evidence.
Given continued weak signals plus high regulatory, ethical, and customer-acceptance risk around passenger profiling in Germany and the EU, the expected value of continuing now appears too low.
The web platform remains closely connected to the firm's established document and travel-security services, and its digital format makes it a relatively low-cost option worth retaining.
